content.comment_body: I am working with an off-delay timer which can be adjusted through the display. By default, the timer is preset to 99 hours in the program, and after a power cycle, it resets to this default value. The issue is, if I set the off-delay to 1 hour and let it run its course, the next time I use it, it retains the 1-hour setting. I’m looking for a solution that automatically resets the timer to the default (99 hours) after completing its countdown, without removing the option to set the time from the display.
Here’s one approach you could consider (please refer to the included image and animation).

Just a note: If you are referencing the initial timer value, the maximum supported time base is in minutes rather than hours. Therefore, you’ll need to input both the default value and any custom (once-off) value in minutes via the display. For example, 99 hours translates to 5940 minutes (99 * 60 = 5940), so you’d need to enter 5940.

I’ve attached my recommended solution. You can continue entering Default and Once-Off timer values in the hh:mm format through the display. When you modify the timer to a once-off value, the system automatically switches to that setting. After the timer finishes, it reverts to the default value. There’s also a screen video included in the attachment for further reference.

Thanks for the prompt response. I’ve implemented your suggestion and it works well. Since working with minutes is sufficient for this scenario, the simpler solution works, but I appreciate knowing the more advanced method for future needs.

analysis.insight_summary: Participants discussed the off-delay timer that can be customized via the display, and that by default, it resets to a preset value after a power cycle. The conversation focused on enabling the timer to revert to its default value automatically after completion, while keeping the manual adjustment feature available. Contributors also clarified details about the input time format and system limitations, offering solutions that accommodate user requirements for both flexibility and reliability.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the timer to automatically reset to its preset default value after finishing the countdown, but still be able to manually adjust the timer value through the display.
